Mis-Communication.summary: Information exists but does not travel intact. The fix is almost never 'communicate more' -- it is fewer, clearer channels with someone standing at each handover.
diagnoseFirst: Map one real message's journey: field incident -> who heard first -> who wrote what -> who never found out
List every channel in use (WhatsApp groups, meetings, registers, calls) and what each is actually FOR -- overlap is the disease
Find where messages die: the person who receives but does not pass on (usually overload, not intent)
Check language switches: field speaks Hindi, reports written in English -- meaning leaks at every translation
rootCauses: Too many channels, none owned
No agreed 'this goes there' rule
Handovers with nobody at the receiving end
Language/format switches mid-journey

interventions.d: Each message type gets ONE home (incidents -> this group; decisions -> this register). Kill duplicate channels rather than adding new ones.
Every handover gets a named receiver who confirms receipt -- the missing task, not a missing person.
The existing recurring meeting gets a fixed 10-minute 'what moved, what stalled' slot -- land the new habit on the meeting that already exists.

indicators: Days for a field incident to reach the office (count 3 real cases)
Messages in the main group per day vs decisions recorded per week
Staff who can name where a given message type belongs (ask 5)
Mis-Communication.watchFor: If they ask for a communication POLICY document, resist -- a policy nobody reads is how this issue got here. Build the habit first, write it down after it works.

Project In-efficiency.summary: Work happens but slowly, with rework. Look for the invisible queue -- where tasks wait, not where people are slow.
diagnoseFirst: Pick one recent project and timeline it backwards: where did days disappear? Waiting beats working as the usual thief
Count the hands one deliverable passes through and what each hand adds
Find rework: what gets done twice, and why (unclear brief? late feedback? format rejected?)
Check the approval bottleneck: how many things wait on ONE person's yes
rootCauses: Approvals funnelled through one person
Unclear briefs causing rework
No visible status -- things wait because nobody sees them waiting
Deadlines without owners

interventions.d: Below a defined size, the doer decides; above it, one named approver with a 48-hour rule. Frees the founder AND the queue.
One shared list (paper or ClickUp): task / owner / waiting-on / due. The point is making waiting VISIBLE, not the tool.
Nothing starts without three lines: what, for whom, done-when. Kills rework at the source.

indicators: Days from task assigned to task done (3 real recent tasks)
Rework count last month (things done twice)
Items currently waiting on a single approver
Project In-efficiency.watchFor: Efficiency drives can read as blame to overloaded staff. Frame everything as 'freeing your time', never 'making you faster' -- and mean it.

Lack of team Management.summary: People work hard but as individuals, not a team. Usually a missing management LAYER or rhythm, not missing management SKILL.
diagnoseFirst: Who actually manages whom? Draw it from behaviour (who do people ask when stuck), not the org chart
Does any manager have TIME to manage, or is management everyone's second job?
Find the rhythm: is there any regular moment where work is reviewed and help is offered? Or only crisis calls?
Ask each senior person: who are you developing? Silence is the answer
rootCauses: Founder manages everyone directly (span too wide)
Managers promoted but never given time or backing
No review rhythm -- management happens only when things break
Nobody develops second-line people

interventions.d: 2-3 coordinators with NAMED people, real say, and protected time -- the VSS pattern: a 6-person cadre replaced founder-does-everything.
One fixed slot per team: what happened, what's stuck, who needs help. Same day, same time, 30 minutes, no cancellations for a month.
Per coordinator: decides alone / decides with founder / passes up. Clarity of authority IS the management training.

indicators: Questions escalated to the founder per week
Staff who can name their direct manager (ask everyone)
Coordinator decisions made without founder sign-off last month
Lack of team Management.watchFor: The founder must VISIBLY route questions back to coordinators or the second line dies in a fortnight. Coach the founder's behaviour first -- the team follows what the founder does, not what the chart says.

Lack of role Clarity.summary: Everyone does everything, so key things belong to nobody. The dangerous version: it FEELS like flexibility and loyalty, so nobody names it as a problem.
diagnoseFirst: Ask 3 people to describe THEIR OWN job in one sentence, then their colleague's -- mismatches map the fog
List work that fell through last quarter: whose was it? 'Everyone's' means nobody's
Check the mirror image: what do TWO people both believe they own (duplicated effort, quiet turf friction)
Test measurement: are people judged on outcomes, or on being busy and present?
rootCauses: Grew from 3 people to 15 without ever dividing work
Roles written once for a funder, never used
Fear that clear roles = rigid hierarchy
Measurement by presence, not output

interventions.d: Whole team, one wall: every recurring task -> one owner -> one backup. Done WITH them in an afternoon, not written FOR them in a week.
Each role gets 2-3 output statements (what exists because this role exists). Replaces task lists that read like chores.
Anything new gets an owner in the same meeting it is born, or it does not start.

indicators: Tasks on the ownership map with a named owner (before: count the unowned)
Items dropped/late last month because ownership was unclear
People who can state their 2-3 outputs unprompted
Lack of role Clarity.watchFor: Role clarity work surfaces buried conflicts -- two people discover they both 'own' the same thing. Expect one hard conversation; schedule it deliberately with both present, don't let it happen in the corridor.

Workflow Issue.summary: The work is understood but its PATH is broken -- steps missing, orders wrong, formats dying between desks. Fix the path, not the people.
diagnoseFirst: Walk ONE real item through its whole path physically -- sit where it sits, see what each hand does to it
Find the format breaks: where does content get retyped, restructured, translated? Each break loses a day and some truth
Find the missing step: the handover where nobody checks what came out the other side (the 'last look' that belongs to no one)
Check the graveyard: which past workflow fixes died, and what killed them
rootCauses: Workflow grew by accretion -- nobody ever designed it
Steps exist because they always did (nobody remembers why)
Format changes mid-path force retyping
No owner for the path itself, only for pieces

interventions.d: Map current path with the people who run it -> mark waits, breaks, retypes -> remove before adding. The smallest path that works.
The field version IS the office version IS the funder version, designed once with all three readers in mind.
One person owns the whole path and takes the last look at the output -- ten minutes that catches what three careful people each assumed another had checked.

indicators: Steps in the current path vs redesigned path (count them)
Times content is retyped/reformatted along the way
Days end-to-end for one real item (3 cases, before and after)
Workflow Issue.watchFor: Never remove a step without asking what invisible purpose it serves -- some 'pointless' steps are quietly protecting against a past disaster. Ask 'what would break?' before cutting.
